articles.title: Rochdale woman loses over 12 stone and reaches Slimming World semi-finals
articles.excerpt: Vikki Gurney from Rochdale has lost 12 stone 3 pounds and reached the semi-finals of Slimming World’s Woman of the Year competition, meeting Olympic champion Nicola Adams in the process.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale woman has achieved a remarkable weight loss of 12 stone 3 pounds, leading her to the semi-finals of Slimming World’s Woman of the Year competition. Vikki Gurney, 39, was selected to represent her Cutgate group after her inspiring transformation from 22 stone 1 pound to 9 stone 12 pounds.

The semi-finals took place at Slimming World’s head office in Derbyshire, where Vikki had the opportunity to meet double Olympic boxing champion Nicola Adams. Vikki's journey began after she saw a photograph of herself at a friend's wedding, prompting her to join the Slimming World group.

Vikki credits her success to a supportive community and a sustainable eating plan that allowed her to enjoy her favourite foods without feeling deprived. She highlighted the importance of weekly meetings with her consultant, Alyson Hartley, and fellow members, which provided her with encouragement and new ideas for meal preparation.

This achievement not only reflects Vikki's personal commitment to health and well-being but also serves as an inspiration for others in the Rochdale community. Her story underscores the positive impact of support networks in weight loss journeys and the importance of finding a plan that fits one's lifestyle.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Rochdale woman loses more than 12 stone and reaches national competition semi-finals | Roch Valley Radio On Air Live now — track details aren't available right now Listen Live Watch Rochdale woman loses more than 12 stone and reaches national competition semi-finals David Murphy News Editor October 22, 2026 | 10:03 PM Print A Rochdale woman who lost 12st 3lb has met double Olympic boxing champion Nicola Adams after reaching the semi-finals of Slimming World’s Woman of the Year competition. Vikki Gurney, 39, was one of 38 women to reach the national semi-finals, held at the organisation’s head office in Derbyshire. Members of her Cutgate group voted for her to represent them in the 2026 competition after she reduced her weight from 22st 1lb to 9st 12lb. Vikki said seeing a photograph of herself at a friend’s wedding prompted her to join the group. She said losing weight had helped her feel more confident about taking part in activities with her children. “For the first time, I found an eating plan that worked with real life. I never felt deprived, and I didn't have to give up the foods I loved.” Vikki said she changed how she prepared meals and found encouragement through weekly meetings with other members and consultant Alyson Hartley. “The support and encouragement I received each week gave me the confidence to keep going. I always come away with new ideas.” She also joined a gym, took up running and completed a Race for Life 10k this summer. Nicola Adams praised Vikki’s achievement when they met at the semi-finals. She said, “Reaching the national semi-finals is a fantastic achievement and Vikki should feel enormously proud of how far she's come.” The Cutgate Slimming World group meets at Cutgate Baptist Church. articles.title: Significant police presence at Cutgate Precinct
articles.excerpt: A significant police presence has been reported at Cutgate Precinct this evening. Details are still emerging and this story will be updated.
articles.content_html:
A significant police presence has been reported at Cutgate Precinct this evening.

Multiple officers were seen in the area of the precinct outside Miami Crispy, and residents nearby have reported ongoing police activity.

The nature of the incident has not yet been confirmed, and Greater Manchester Police has not released a statement at the time of publication.

This is a developing story and will be updated as soon as verified information becomes available. If you were in the area and have information, you can contact Greater Manchester Police on 101, or 999 in an emergency.
